the structure, dynamics, and function of proteins that bind to heme.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have discovered a new family of sugar-binding proteins, the DOMON proteins.

we have identified a novel protein domain (the DOMON domain) that is present in a large and diverse group of bacterial proteins that are involved in the transport and metabolism of sugars, heme and other small organic molecules.
we have discovered a new family of heme-binding proteins and have identified a heme-binding domain, which we call the heme-associated domain of the membrane (HADom).

the DOMON domains are not just a simple sugar binding module, but a versatile module that is involved in a variety of functions including heme and sugar binding.
